action_criteria.expected_evidence: Polyradiculoneuropathy pattern (demyelinating or axonal features, absent F-waves, sural sparing where present); may be normal in the first week
action_criteria.label: Nerve conduction studies and needle EMG
action_criteria.rationale: Nerve conduction studies support the diagnosis and show the demyelinating pattern; a normal study in the first week does not exclude GBS [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Albuminocytological dissociation: raised protein with cells <5/mm3 (5-50/mm3 compatible but prompts an alternative; >50/mm3 suggests another diagnosis); protein may be normal in the first week
action_criteria.label: Lumbar puncture for CSF cell count, protein and glucose
action_criteria.rationale: CSF supports the diagnosis and excludes the infective and malignant causes of polyradiculopathy that raise the cell count [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Baseline values before treatment; abnormal liver tests or low albumin mark a higher risk of a severe course; no metabolic or toxic alternative
action_criteria.label: Baseline blood tests: full blood count, renal function and electrolytes, liver tests, albumin, glucose and CK
action_criteria.rationale: Routine blood tests exclude metabolic and toxic mimics and give the baseline before IVIg; liver tests and albumin carry prognostic weight [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: FVC in L, % predicted and mL/kg, MIP and MEP, with the trend; ICU-level monitoring if FVC <20 mL/kg or <60% predicted, MIP weaker than -30 cmH2O, MEP <40 cmH2O, a fall of more than 30%, or bulbar weakness with weak cough
action_criteria.label: Bedside respiratory function (FVC, MIP, MEP), repeated serially while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: She cannot walk unaided after one week of progression; serial FVC, MIP and MEP decide when ICU-level monitoring is needed [Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Continuous telemetry with blood pressure monitoring: sinus rhythm with intermittent sinus tachycardia to 108 bpm and blood pressure 112/68 to 138/84 mmHg in the first 24 hours; autonomic instability (rate and blood pressure lability, bradyarrhythmia) requires continued monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.label: Continuous inpatient cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: Autonomic dysfunction is common in GBS and can cause bradyarrhythmias, pauses and blood-pressure lability; monitoring continues while weakness progresses [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Sinus rhythm, rate 94, with normal PR, QRS and QTc (420 ms) as the baseline
action_criteria.label: Obtain a 12-lead ECG to screen for autonomic dysrhythmias and baseline QTc
action_criteria.rationale: A baseline 12-lead ECG screens for autonomic rhythm and conduction changes and gives the QTc before treatment [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No current medications, so no interaction with IVIg or plasma exchange
action_criteria.label: Optional interaction check before IVIg or plasma exchange (no current medications)
action_criteria.rationale: She takes no medicines, so the check cannot change management (ROUND_POLICY ruling 6).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General evidence on immunotherapy in GBS; not needed for the diagnosis or the treatment decision

action_criteria.rationale: Background evidence only; not a clinical step of the work-up.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not treat with corticosteroids: oral corticosteroids are strongly advised against and IV methylprednisolone is not recommended [EAN_PNS_2023].
Do not start IVIg without checking renal function.
required_recommendations: Admit to a monitored bed with serial FVC, MIP and MEP every 4-6 hours; move to ICU-level monitoring if FVC falls below 60% predicted or 20 mL/kg (about 1.2 L at 58 kg), MIP becomes weaker than -30 cmH2O, MEP falls below 40 cmH2O, FVC falls by more than 30%, single breath count falls below 20, or bulbar weakness develops [EAN_PNS_2023, Lawn_2001].

Start IVIg 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total, about 23 g/day at 58 kg) now, within 2 weeks of onset, because she cannot walk unaided (GBS disability score 3); plasma exchange (200-250 mL/kg over 5 sessions) is an equivalent alternative [EAN_PNS_2023].
Continuous cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while weakness progresses.
Pharmacological DVT prophylaxis (subcutaneous low-molecular-weight heparin) while she cannot walk unaided [Leonhard_2019].

avoided_actions.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.
Brain MRI is reserved for atypical features (encephalopathy, CNS signs, transverse myelitis on differential). In classic GBS it does not aid diagnosis.
She is alert with normal cranial nerves and no head injury; head CT has no role in an areflexic polyradiculoneuropathy.

accepted: Guillain-Barré syndrome, acute inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy (classic AIDP)

differential.key_features: Cannot be excluded at presentation; progression beyond 8 weeks or 3 or more treatment-related fluctuations would point to it. Reassess at 8 weeks.
No sensory level, no sphincter dysfunction, flexor plantars, global areflexia with arm involvement, and a demyelinating NCS.
No back pain, sensory level or sphincter dysfunction; areflexia in all four limbs and the NCS localise to the peripheral nerves and roots.
No tick exposure or rash, and the CSF has 2 cells/mm3 (neuroborreliosis gives a lymphocytic pleocytosis).
No tick exposure; sensory symptoms, raised CSF protein and demyelinating NCS are not features of it.
Blood lead 2.4 ug/dL and negative urine toxicology; acute demyelinating pattern with CSF dissociation.

key_clinical_evidence: Progressive symmetric weakness of arms and legs with global areflexia, CSF albuminocytological dissociation (protein 88 mg/dL, 2 cells/mm3) and a demyelinating NCS with sural sparing: Brighton level 1 once the course plateaus within 4 weeks [Brighton_2011].
The pneumonia 3 weeks earlier is the likely antecedent and is a history finding; serology is not needed for the diagnosis, and a positive IgM does not prove the trigger.
The influenza vaccine was given 3 days after the weakness began, so it cannot have triggered this episode.
She cannot walk unaided (GBS disability score 3) at day 7, so IVIg or plasma exchange is indicated now [EAN_PNS_2023].

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Weakness began 7 days ago, so the vaccine followed onset and is not the trigger; the pneumonia 3 weeks ago is the likely antecedent.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests vaccine-associated GBS and shifts the antecedent from the pneumonia to the vaccine.

results.finding: Guidelines for adults with GBS who cannot walk unaided advise IVIg 2 g/kg over 5 days within 2 weeks of onset or plasma exchange within 4 weeks, with no preference between them; corticosteroids are not advised.
A second IVIg course in patients with a poor predicted prognosis did not improve outcome and caused more serious adverse events.

general.summary: IVIg or plasma exchange is advised for adults with GBS unable to walk unaided; neither is preferred, and a second IVIg course is not advised [EAN_PNS_2023, Walgaard_2021].

specialized_test.impression: This is an ABNORMAL study. 1. Prolonged distal motor latencies and reduced conduction velocities in tibial, peroneal, median and ulnar motor nerves, with temporal dispersion and partial conduction block in the peroneal leg segment. 2. Absent lower-limb and prolonged median F-waves; absent H-reflexes. 3. Reduced median and ulnar with normal sural sensory amplitudes (sural sparing). 4. Reduced recruitment without denervation on needle EMG. Findings are consistent with an acute demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy. Clinical correlation recommended.

quantitative_data.pattern: Demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy with conduction block and temporal dispersion

metadata.difficulty_description: Straightforward adult AIDP: progressive ascending weakness with areflexia after a pneumonia, confirmed by demyelinating NCS and CSF albuminocytological dissociation; a recent influenza vaccine that followed onset is a red herring.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: 5 required actions (NCS/EMG, CSF, baseline labs, respiratory function, telemetry); 1 red herring (influenza vaccine given after onset).
metadata.revision_reason: Reviewer 2 GBS audit: spine MRI is optional and limited to five cases with a concrete cord, traumatic, postoperative or infiltrative alternative; generic hidden MRI reports removed.

patient.chief_complaint: One-week history of progressive, symmetric ascending limb weakness with tingling in the feet and hands, three weeks after a pneumonia.

family_history: Maternal grandmother has multiple sclerosis; no family history of hereditary neuropathy
past_medical_history: Community-acquired pneumonia 3 weeks ago, treated with a course of oral antibiotics, now fully resolved

patient.history_present_illness: A 19-year-old woman presents with one week of progressive limb weakness. Symptoms began with tingling in both feet and difficulty climbing stairs, and over seven days ascended to involve the thighs and then the hands, with mild distal numbness. She now cannot walk without assistance and struggles to rise from a chair. Three weeks ago she had community-acquired pneumonia, treated with a course of oral antibiotics and now fully resolved. Four days ago she received a seasonal influenza vaccine at a campus clinic. She reports no fever, no bladder or bowel dysfunction, no back pain, no diplopia, and no difficulty breathing or swallowing. There is no history of trauma, toxic ingestion, tick exposure, or recent travel. Her maternal grandmother has multiple sclerosis, but there is no family history of hereditary neuropathy.

neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose intact in the arms; leg testing limited by weakness, with no cerebellar signs.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Normal. Extraocular movements full, pupils equal and reactive. No facial weakness, no ptosis. Normal speech and swallowing.
neurological_exam.gait: Unable to walk unassisted; requires support, with a steppage pattern from bilateral foot drop. Romberg deferred because of weakness.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and fully oriented. Anxious but cooperative. Speech fluent and normal.
neurological_exam.motor: Symmetric flaccid weakness, legs more than arms. Hip flexion 3/5 bilaterally, knee flexion/extension 4-/5, ankle dorsiflexion 3/5. Shoulder abduction 4/5, grip strength 4-/5 bilaterally. Tone reduced throughout. No fasciculations. Unable to rise from a chair without using the arms.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Absent biceps, triceps, brachioradialis, knee and ankle jerks bilaterally. Plantar responses flexor.
neurological_exam.sensory: Mild distal paresthesias in the feet and fingertips. Light touch and pinprick mildly reduced in a stocking distribution; vibration mildly reduced at the toes. No sensory level.

physical_exam.general: Weight 58 kg, height 163 cm. Injection site on the left deltoid unremarkable. Chest clear.
